messages:
sophia-cs: Heads up — Customer (acct: corp-alpha) hit constant 429s during a live demo this morning. They say it started at 09:12 PT and persisted despite retries. Payload is bulk embeddings (~500 docs) sent in parallel. They are on the free tier.

sophia-cs: Key details from customer:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- API key id: sk-***-corp-alpha
- Error body: { \"error\": { \"message\": \"Rate limit exceeded\", \"type\": \"rate_limit_error\" }}
- Response headers they saw: X-RateLimit-Limit: 600/min, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 30

zack-oncall: Thanks — can you paste the request pattern? i.e., concurrency, batch_size, doc size?

sophia-cs: They said ~20 parallel requests with batch_size 25, avg doc size ~1.2k tokens. Happened right as they started a scheduled ingest for a product demo.

raj-engineering: 20x25 ~500 docs at once, that will blow straight through free-tier per-minute tokens. Free plan has burst headroom but not sustained concurrency. Suggest immediate mitigations:
- Drop concurrency to 2-3 workers
- Increase batch_size to reduce calls (if memory ok) or the opposite? actually for embeddings larger batch reduces reqs but may increase per-request token count; balance for their token usage.
- Add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s

sophia-cs: I sent them a quick how-to for backoff + sample curl with Retry-After handling. They replied that they need the demo in 45 minutes and asked if we can temporarily raise their limits for the window.

liam-sales: If they want temporary burst we can do a short-term upgrade/exception. For free-tier customers we usually offer a 24-48h paid trial or a one-time temporary quota raise tied to a CC. Need approval from billing for exceptions under $500.

emma-billing: I can approve a one-time quota increase for demos, but need written customer consent and we must document chargeable hours. Also need their account email and company billing contact.

sophia-cs: Provided contact: billing@corp-alpha.com. Customer asked for a same-day increase to 2x token rate for 3 hours. 

raj-engineering: Operationally we can create a short-lived quota override flag (quota_override: {tokens_per_minute: XXX, expires_at: epoch}). It requires an ops ticket and a backend toggle. On the runtime side we can route them to a higher burst pool if capacity exists. I can do the toggle if approved.

quota-bot: Incident note created: INC-2027-4537 — temporary quota override request for acct corp-alpha. Assigned to raj-engineering.

zack-oncall: Quick Q — is this purely rate limit or also auth? sometimes clients spin keys and hit 401s during mass runs. Sophia, did customer report any 401/403?

sophia-cs: No 401s, only 429 and the body clearly says rate limit. They forwarded the X-RateLimit headers which match.

raj-engineering: For transparency, the backend supports two knobs: tokens_per_minute and burst_capacity. I can set tokens_per_minute to 2x their current for 3 hours and bump burst_capacity +20%. But we need billing ok and a rollback time.

liam-sales: We should offer a commercial path: a one-week pro trial (paid) that automatically ups quotas and gives SLA for the demo. If they go pro we can credit the demo charges toward first invoice. This avoids manual hourly approvals later.

emma-billing: OK if customer agrees to a CC on file we can spin a pro trial and apply a promo code. Ask them to confirm. Meanwhile, we can approve a temporary free-tier exception capped at $200 in overage to be invoiced if they exceed.

sophia-cs: I asked the customer to confirm whether they'd prefer a short paid trial vs a manual exception. They replied: 'We can't put a card on file for the demo. Need a free one-time bump to run the demo.'

zack-oncall: Policy note — we rarely do free permanent increases. For trust and audit we can do a 3-hour free temporary override but flag for follow-up to sales. If accepted, raj — can you do the toggle now?

raj-engineering: I can. Please get an explicit written acknowledgement (Slack DM or email) from the customer agreeing to the temporary free bump and that they'll be contacted by sales after. Once I have that I will:
1) create override: tokens_per_minute = current * 2
2) set expires_at = now + 3 hours (epoch: 179450... approximate)
3) add audit log entry and notify ops via /incident update

sophia-cs: Customer sent this message: 'Corp Alpha agrees to a one-time free 3-hour quota bump for demo at 11:00 PT, and we consent to be contacted by sales after. — alice@corp-alpha.com' I pasted the email thread into the ticket.

raj-engineering: On it. Applying override now. Pasting CLI toggle: 
```
# internal admin api
POST /internal/v1/accounts/corp-alpha/quotas/override
Authorization: Bearer admin-***
{ "tokens_per_minute": 1200, "burst_capacity": 300, "expires_at": 179450... }
```

quota-bot: Quota override applied by raj-engineering. Override id: qov-91234. Expires in 3h.

sophia-cs: Customer retested at 11:05 PT — initial reply: \"Embeds running, earlier 429s gone, thank you!\" :tada:

zack-oncall: Great. Please monitor for any unexpected cost spikes. I will trace logs for that account and confirm no backend throttling occurred.

emma-billing: I logged a provisional invoice hold. Since this is free temporary, set flag 'sales-followup' so we reach out next business day.

liam-sales: I'll own follow-up. I'll put a short outreach sequence and offer the one-week paid trial with promo credit.

raj-engineering: Postmortem notes — customer was triggering concurrency limit more than sustained per-minute tokens. Recommended long-term fixes:
- Move ingestion to dedicated capacity or upgrade plan
- Implement client-side concurrency caps and proper backoff
- Use batching to optimize tokens-per-call and reduce per-minute request count

sophia-cs: Closing loop: Customer confirmed demo success at 11:42 PT. I'll update support ticket and add notes: temporary override qov-91234 applied, no charges, sales follow-up scheduled.

zack-oncall: Adding final verification: I pulled runtime traces — no other customer impact, override used existing spare capacity. Marking incident resolved.

sophia-cs: Thanks team. Lesson: we should add a quick-run checklist for demo requests (small doc) so CS can propose immediate mitigations before asking for overrides. I'll draft that and ping product for a short KB entry. :memo:

liam-sales: I'll add a templated offer (one-week trial + promo) to make sales handoffs faster.

quota-bot: INC-2027-4537 resolved. Audit link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2027-4537
